newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga's Snorre oilfield hits record 250,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Saga's Snorre oilfield hits record 250,000 bpd.

text.p: Crude output at the North Sea Snorre oilfield hit a record 250,000 barrels per day (bpd) in early December, operator Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday.

The field hit peak production on December 7 following an overhaul of processing systems on the Statfjord A platform and the debottlenecking of the Snorre plant during regular maintenance in the spring, Saga said in its weekly newsletter.
Crude from Snorre is piped to Statoil's Statfjord A installation for processing and loading at offshore loading buoys.
"Four principle factors determine the volume produced," said Hans Morten Stroemmevold, Saga's production vice president.

"The wells must deliver from the reservoir, the platform processing plant must be able to handle that flow, the export line to Statfjord A must have enough capacity and the A platform must be in a position to accept what Snorre produces," he said.
Seven subsea and 14 platform wells now flow on Snorre.
Stroemmevold said everything was in place to reach the company's production goal for Snorre.
